metadata.name: C172N
metadata.copyrightInfo: © 2026 Flying Particles, Inc. For Flying Particles club use only. Expanded checklist for instruction based on the 1977 Cessna 172N POH, STC SA1945CE supplement POH-7701 (11 Nov 88) and the FPI Cessna 172N Checkout Form rev. 11/2026

items.prompt: # reflects an entry on the C172N checkout form rev. 11/2026.
STC SA1945CE (Powerflow exhaust) raises max weight to 2,400 lb. Flaps 30° max (not 40°).
The Dynon EFIS and Century IIB autopilot are placarded INOP. No manifold pressure gauge: set power by RPM.
The winterization kit placard is legacy: no kit is fitted.
STC speeds override the POH. Sea level speeds: checkout form. 10,000 ft and approach: POH.
FLOW: cockpit, then tail, right wing, nose, left wing, final look. Fuel and oil every flight.
Gauges can be off by a gallon or two: look in the tanks.
Drain before the first flight of the day and after every refueling. Look for water (bubbles or clear globs) and dirt.
Club rule: add one quart when it falls to 5 quarts. POH: never fly below 4 quarts, fill to 6 for extended flights.
Check the stall warning by gentle suction with a cloth; the horn should sound.
Use the full prime when cold, none when hot. Lock the primer in before starting.
Sky-Tec starter placard: crank 10 seconds max, cool 20 seconds between tries, up to 6 tries, then cool 30 minutes.
No oil pressure in 30 seconds: shut down. Twice that in very cold weather.
The GDL 88 self tests at power up and shows failures as annunciations (Garmin ICA 190-01310-01).
Avoid carburetor heat after starting unless icing conditions exist.
Weak firing and black smoke from the exhaust mean overprimed or flooded.
As soon as the cylinders fire, open the throttle slightly to keep it running.
Club practice: lean on the ground to avoid plug fouling. Rich again for the runup.
Compass swings, turn coordinator turns the correct way, attitude erect, ball moves.
Differential between mags 50 RPM maximum. Smooth operation on each.
Expect an RPM drop with heat on. Full cold should restore the RPM.
Oil pressure 25 psi minimum, 100 psi maximum (green 60 to 90). Oil temperature 245°F maximum.
Flaps 0° to 10° are approved for takeoff. Flaps more than 10° are not.
Static RPM at full throttle: 2280 to 2400. Rough or slow to accelerate: abort.
Use 10° flaps for short and soft fields. Leave them out until the obstacle is cleared, then retract as you accelerate.
Cruise climb is 5 to 10 knots above Vy for visibility and cooling.
Lean until RPM peaks, then enrich until RPM drops 25 to 50. Above 75% power lean only to peak RPM.
The single-probe EGT is not an engine monitor: trust RPM. Fuel selector BOTH keeps the tanks balanced.
Apply carburetor heat before closing the throttle.
Flaps 10° or less below 110 KIAS, 10° to 30° below 85 KIAS.
Placard: avoid slips with flaps extended. POH: avoid steep slips above 20° flaps (elevator oscillation).
Control wheel full aft, brake hard without skidding.
Trim for climb at once. A landing trim setting pitches the nose up at full power.
Refuel if over 1 tach hour since last fill. Selector LEFT or RIGHT while refueling (POH), BOTH at preflight.
Unexplained RPM drop is the sign. Use minimum heat to prevent re-icing and readjust the mixture.
Low pressure with normal temperature may be the gauge, but land to find out.
The over-voltage relay trips at about 16 V.
Airspeed and altimeter may read slightly differently on alternate static; see the POH for corrections.
Land straight ahead. Use only gentle turns to avoid obstacles.
If the propeller is windmilling, the engine will restart on its own when fuel and ignition are restored.
The basic POH recommends 40° flaps. With the STC the maximum is 30°.
The aim is to draw flames and fuel into the engine.
Do not restart. Overhead vents may stay open.
Power needed: master ON, check breakers (do not reset), switch equipment on one at a time.
Open the left window, use a forward slip, and expect a higher stall speed.
